# Deliver

Write from what the ontology holds, cite it, and give back what you learned. `O` is `python3 plugins/general-ontology/bin/onto`, run from the topic repo root; prefer the `onto_*` MCP tools when this harness has them. Follow the reading rules of the **onto**
skill.

## 1. One call

Call `onto_context task="<the task in the user's words>"`, plus `deliverable=<template>` when the user names one
(`O context "write the weekly menu"`). It returns the goals, the constraints, the active decisions for the scope, the
template's section headings with the ids for each, the subject nodes and the open gaps, within a budget of 1000
tokens. Without a named template it picks the one whose sections fit the task best, else `brief`. Each goal line
already carries its key attributes (horizon, success) and the metrics that measure it with their targets, so no
follow-up `onto_get` on a goal is needed. Each subject line is followed by `linked <subject> <label> <id>: <summary>`
lines, the records one hop from it; write from them.

## 2. Follow up only where needed

Each `left out to fit N tokens` entry names the exact call for what it left out. Make a call only when the
deliverable needs that part (a quote you will cite, a section with too few facts).

A subject's linked records left out show as `N linked records (onto get <id>, also ...)` in the left-out line, or as
`linked <subject>: +N more (onto get <subject>)`. When the deliverable is about that subject, make those calls before
writing, and never write "none in the ontology" for something the subject line counts (for example `defines 3`).

## 3. Write

- Title, then the version line in italics under it, verbatim.
- Keep every template heading, in order. Under a heading with nothing in the ontology, write "none in the ontology".
  A decisions heading that reads `none for this scope (N active: onto decisions)` means no active decision covers
  this deliverable: write that, not "none in the ontology", which you write only where context prints it.
- Cite ids in backticks for every claim: `kitchen/deliverable:weekly-menu`. Cite only ids the kit printed.
- Mark drafts as drafts and keep `[untrusted]` on quotes from ingested sources.
- End with two sections: **Active decisions** (id, the choice, one line each) and **Open points** (the gaps and
  questions the context listed: take the `open:` lines; an `open: +N more:` line names an `onto gaps --node` call
  for the rest).
- State facts plainly. What the ontology does not hold is an open point, not a guess.

A finished example is in `references/worked-example.md`.

## 4. Give back what you learned

Anything new that came up while writing (a fact the user told you, a term you had to define, a link you found in a
source) goes back as a proposal: `onto_propose` with `by: "agent"`, each op with a quote and a `loc` (`L<a>-L<b>` of
the source). What the user told you needs a source first: `onto_answer` when it answers an interview question (leave
`src` and `loc` out; the kit fills in the answer's source and `Q:<question id>`, the id before any `@`), else
`onto_ingest text=...` of their words. Link each new node in the same proposal (a new term gets a `defines` edge).
Then hand off to **onto-review**. Never edit the topic files directly.
